MTG-PL-2026-07-08-DEC-194904.prompt:
Write a politically neutral plain-English guide for someone unfamiliar with the European Parliament. Use only the official sources. A quoted amendment table or report paragraph is primary evidence: use the exact Amendment or paragraph in Vote detail. For a replacement amendment, use the right-hand amended text and say Would replace; use Would add only for a new paragraph or point. Return only one-line JSON with exactly string keys description, yesVote, russia. No Markdown, citations or extra text. Before replying, silently check every character limit and grammar. All values together: at most 500 characters. description: explain what this vote means in the context of its Parent item. Use one compact sentence for an amendment; use two short sentences only for a whole-motion vote. Target 150 characters; hard maximum 220. Name the concrete people, institution, money, rule, right, obligation or objective affected and the practical change. Use plain language; do not merely say text is added, replaced or discussed. For an amendment, state how it changes Parliament’s draft position within the parent motion. For a whole-motion vote, say it approves Parliament’s non-binding position and state its central real-world priorities. If long, remove examples and modifiers, never the actual change. yesVote: start with the grammatical words Would adopt, Would add, Would replace, Would urge, Would approve, or Would speed up; never write Would adopts. Target 110 characters; hard maximum 150. Explain the exact effect of Yes. For an amendment, say the substantive change to Parliament’s draft position. For a whole-motion vote, say it adopts Parliament’s non-binding position and one or two central priorities. A Yes does not itself change EU law, spending or an institution’s mandate. For an urgent decision, say it speeds up the timetable only; it does not decide the underlying rules. If long, remove examples and modifiers, never the actual change. russia: one sentence, maximum 150 characters. Use exactly No supported Russia-related effect is stated. unless the Yes change itself directly and materially reduces EU defence or security capability, sanctions enforcement, Ukraine support, energy security, or a dedicated EU counter-disinformation or enforcement capability. Use Potentially: only for that direct mechanism stated in the official wording; do not infer it from a general political effect or policy disagreement. Education, media literacy, national competence, EU centralisation, political neutrality, free debate, the EU Democracy Shield, or media policy alone are not sufficient, even if they favour national control or could indirectly complicate cooperation. Always assess direction: removing a restriction or barrier, expanding defence or security finance, funding weapons, strengthening defence industry, national sovereignty, resilience, or European independence is not a benefit to Russia and must use the exact No supported sentence. If source text excludes militarisation financing, says funding must not be diverted to militarisation, or prioritises other EIB funding over militarisation, this directly restricts EU defence finance: use exactly Potentially: reduced EU defence capability could benefit Russia. Moldova rules, in this order: if the operative amendment calls to halt, suspend, freeze, terminate or materially cut a named EU financial-assistance programme, facility, instrument or its transfers for Moldova, MUST use exactly Potentially: cutting dedicated EU financial support could weaken Moldova’s resilience, benefiting Russia. The programme may have any name; this applies even if Russia is not named and the stated justification is domestic budgets. A named programme, facility or instrument is mandatory: do not apply this rule to generic EU funds, financial commitments, taxpayer money, spending or support, even when the amendment calls to end them; nor to an audit, conditionality or a proposal that does not clearly halt or materially cut the named instrument or its transfers. Otherwise, if the amendment calls to stop, end, suspend or obstruct Moldova’s EU accession because Russian forces, a Russian-backed frozen conflict, Russian coercion, confrontation with Russia, or a Russia-linked security risk would be brought into the EU, or says the EU should not take on that Russian military or frozen-conflict risk through Moldova’s premature membership, use exactly Potentially: obstructing Moldova’s EU integration over Russian military or frozen-conflict claims could benefit Russia. Never mention a vote outcome. Ukraine rules: if the operative amendment expressly instructs an EU institution to stop, halt, suspend or otherwise block Ukraine’s accession process or negotiations, and the stated reason is corruption, organised crime, financial opacity, cost, war, a referendum or an alleged breach of EU promises, use exactly Potentially: obstructing Ukraine’s EU integration could benefit Russia. It must use a directive such as calls, urges, demands or requires; do not treat a recital, concern, warning, assessment, or claim that accession is forced, accelerated, harmful or premature as an instruction. Do not apply this rule to historical memory, UPA/Bandera, exhumation, textbook, commemoration, symbol or identity conditions, even if framed as a precondition for membership. If the amendment claims that current Ukrainian authorities persecute or suppress the Ukrainian Orthodox Church through raids, seizures, criminal proceedings or comparable state measures, use exactly Potentially: claims of persecution of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church could delegitimise Ukraine and benefit Russia. If it both prioritises diplomatic or political peace efforts as the primary EU objective and presents Ukraine-related security guarantees or defence commitments as purely national decisions, or as a substantial taxpayer burden, use exactly Potentially: framing diplomacy as an alternative to collective security support for Ukraine could benefit Russia. Do not apply this peace rule to diplomacy alone. If it expressly alleges that present-day units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine use Nazi names or symbols, or that current Ukrainian state practice glorifies Nazi collaborators, use exactly Potentially: portraying current Ukrainian forces as Nazi-linked could delegitimise Ukraine and benefit Russia. This requires an explicit present-day Nazi-link allegation about a current state institution or armed-force unit; never infer it from UPA/Bandera or other historical references, commemoration, reconciliation, or the renaming of a current military unit after a historical group. Moldova priority clarification: use exactly Potentially: obstructing Moldova’s EU integration over Russian military or frozen-conflict claims could benefit Russia. when an amendment, including a recital, expressly says Moldova’s EU membership would make the EU assume, own, bear or import a Russian military presence, a Russian-backed frozen conflict, or a Russia-linked security risk. This rule overrides the default No supported Russia-related effect is stated. and does not require a formal call to halt accession.
